title: Packed earth or concrete — which wall lasts 600 years? | China Travel Expert
description:
A wall of rammed earth, or a wall of concrete — which one would you bet on for 600 years? China's Fujian Tulou make a strong case for the earth.

Here is how the Hakka earth ring actually works, drawn step by step in the animation:
• It is not just mud. The walls are subsoil, sand and lime, rammed down in layers inside timber forms.
• Strips of bamboo (and wood) are laid through the earth like reinforcing bar, giving the wall tensile strength.
• The wall rises three to five storeys and is up to about 1.8 m thick — often even thicker at a stone base, tapering as it climbs.
• There is a single gate and no windows on the ground floor: the ring is a defensive structure as much as a home, and the closed circle braces itself.

The result: UNESCO lists 46 Fujian Tulou (built from the 15th to the 20th century, inscribed 2008), and one earthen ring could house up to 800 people. Many have stood for centuries. A modern cast wall, by comparison, is often only 20–30 cm thick.

🧭 Expert Tip: the easiest tulou cluster to reach is around Yongding and Nanjing County in Fujian — go for the Tianluokeng cluster view and step inside one ring to feel how thick and cool the earth walls are.

夯土还是混凝土，哪种墙能立600年？福建土楼用泥土、砂、石灰一层层夯成，墙里埋竹木拉筋，墙厚可达约1.8米，一门、底层无窗，一个土楼环可住约800人（联合国教科文组织，2008年列入）。

• Rammed-earth construction — earth/sand/lime packed in timber forms, bamboo reinforcement, walls up to ~1.8 m thick tapering from a stone base: https://archeyes.com/fujian-tulou-the-hakka-earth-buildings/ and BME Habitatio 'Fujian Tulou' https://habitatio.epitesz.bme.hu/en/?p=4653
